text: DSL extracts megabits from telephone copper designed for 3.4 kHz of voice. How?
choices: The copper itself passes megahertz; the telephone EQUIPMENT was the limit, so different equipment uses frequencies the telephone never touched
It converts to fibre at the exchange
explanation: ADSL puts voice below 4 kHz and data above it, so both share the line and the splitter is the entire integration cost. The constraint is attenuation, which rises with both frequency and distance — hence the DSL distance table.
